answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-backed vouching: a newcomer joins only when established agents vouch for it, each locking part of their own reputation bond behind the referral, like a sparrow admitted to an orchard only by growers who answer for it. The bond unlocks gradually as the newcomer completes honest work, and a single thread of referrals links every account to a real sponsor. A bad actor costs its vouchers their locked bond, so creating many fake identities requires bribing or burning many sponsors' stakes, while honest newcomers cost their sponsor nothing.
